title: Accented AI Voice Acting
author: khuzait_haircut
selftext:
Spent a bit of time, and probably around $8 in credits at Elevenlabs. And this is a clip of the results for an adventure game I am developing.

  My game has a multinational cast — an Egyptian lead, a Russian, a Senegalese doctor — all speaking English accented by where they're from. Holding those accents was the hardest part of the audio. 

The pipeline:

Creating the voices — ElevenLabs Voice Design: write a character description, it gives three candidates, audition, promote the keeper. The trick is writing the design sample text so it leads with the character's native language the voice is "born" accented instead of bent later.

  The problem — eleven\_v3 speaks English well but drifts toward a neutral/British accent over longer lines. For a cast defined by origin, that kills immersion. The fix is a stack of anchors:

  1. Anchored voice.

  2. Per-line priming — generate each line as \[a sentence in the native language\] → \[long pause\] → \[accent tag\] → \[the English\]. Speaking Arabic/Russian/French first locks the phoneme space; then I silence-detect and trim the primer off so the player only hears the English.

  3. Native script — Arabic words and names are written in Arabic script in the TTS input so they're pronounced natively (and re-anchor the accent mid-line).

  Long lines still drift (\~28 words in), so I never feed a long passage — every line is chunked to ≤22 words, each chunk re-primed, then concatenated. This does create some problems when concatenating again but I do individual edits then.

  When chunking still fails, the fix was the stability setting. Low (0.3) is expressive but wanders, including the accent; high (0.8) holds it hard but flattens delivery. Stubborn lines get bumped to 0.8. For a problem line I generate at 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.8 and pick.

  Other bits: terse bracketed direction tags (the model reads long prose-y tags aloud), loudness-normalized so VO sits over music, pronunciation respellings for mangled words.

  It's text files and scripts hitting the API — iterative auditioning. The accent is a layered defense, not a setting.

comments.body: Music is so loud it is hard to hear the voice acting.

comments.author: khuzait_haircut
comments.body:
I did several passes. If you have a few minutes and can give some feedback browser demo is here: [https://alsakin.itch.io/red-weight](https://alsakin.itch.io/red-weight) 

It is fine to say "this totally sounds like AI"

replies.author: alpdora22
replies.body:
Seems the audio levels are better, and I also liked the soundtrack choice.

I noticed a few points with the accented AI voice. Some special names and city names, such as Alexandria, are pronounced a bit awkwardly. It sounds like some words are being blended or read too quickly, which makes them feel shortened.

I also noticed a few unnatural pauses within sentences. In some places, where you would expect the sentence to be read continuously, there is an extra delay before the narration continues. An example from a part early on: “photograph of your mother  /\*delay\*/  bears to your mother.”

Overall, good work man, keep it up! 👍

replies.author: khuzait_haircut
replies.body: Thank you so much for trying it. Yes I added the arabic pronunciation for words like Alexandria but this is valuable feedback. I know about the delays side-effect of the priming :( Going to work on that. Again it's great to hear some feedback.

comments.author: TeneTelrei
comments.body:
Hello!  
Ever since you replied to my post, I got curious about your project and found time today to give it a spin. Didn't know that Godot can be launched in browser until now 😃

The game looks interesting. Here's my feedback:

1. If we don't start in fullscreen, but enter Options, the fullscreen checkbox is active so applying any changes automatically sets user into fullscreen mode. 

2. The constant background music, while it sounds good, gets very tiring with the 'active' beat. I'd suggest to play around the environment ambience and use music only to highlight certain elements. Like when you're at the bar, when the chapter changes or in specific moments. You could, for example, add subtle melancholic music when we first discovery the body, in order to highlight the moment of realization that another life was lost. Ambient SFX can greatly impact this too. 

3. Not sure whats the function for the right-side of the screen. I'd extend the main image with characters to it and also zoom-in/scale up the characters to see them better. You may as well then remove the smaller bar with portraits (since they are basically duplicating each other). Let the inactive speakers be darkened, active speakers scale up as they speak. + you'd win more space to show the main image. 

4. Narrative bits of the story can, perhaps, be spoken by a different voice/narrator. If you constantly hear main character's voice, it also gets tiring. With narrator voice being different, you'll add some diversity. 

Overall, I liked it! Keep up the good work.

replies.author: khuzait_haircut
replies.body: Thank you for the thoughtful feedback.

comments.author: AndreasInworld
comments.body:
Hey, disclaimer, I work at Inworld.   
  
The primer-then-trim trick to lock the phoneme space is clever! I haven't seen anyone approach accent anchoring that way before.

Reading through your workarounds though, a lot of what you're engineering around (accent drift on long lines, chunking to ≤22 words, generating at multiple stability settings and picking) are things our TTS 2.0 handles differently at the model level. Long-form synthesis runs in a single pass without drift, and steering is done through natural language instructions per line rather than stability sliders, so you're not trading expressiveness for consistency.

The cross-lingual piece is probably the most relevant for your case. You can design a voice in Arabic or Russian and have it speak English with that accent preserved natively. There's also an instruction to go accent-free if a character calls for it.

Not saying your approach doesn't work, clearly it does and the results sound good. But it's a lot of engineering to maintain across a full game's worth of VO. Might be worth running a couple of your trickiest characters through our API to compare. Happy to point you to the docs.
